# surface.offset_surface: measured conditional rounding (2026-11-04)

Updates: plan/findings/surface.offset_surface--default-third-derivatives-diagnostic-attribution--addendum-2026-11-04-per-case-four-term-attribution.md

The 103 cases below contain all 478 changed components in the unresolved-relative-jet group; 258 components across all 103 cases disagree with the independent local jet under the existing 1e-9 relative rule, with no absolute floor. None of these 103 has been listed as `cpp_defect` by the parent; no marker is approved or proposed here. The relative policy is unchanged. These measurements do not establish that a result passes the geometric correctness criterion.

The temporary Python probe replays the corrected normal-derivative recurrence using recorded binary64 base partials and distance, the Rust vector operation order and ordinary binary64 arithmetic, and separately runs the same algebra with Decimal precision 200. All 478 replayed components bit-match the recorded corrected Rust values; all 478 Decimal recurrence values are consistent with an independent 200-digit Taylor-jet calculation. Inputs are converted with `Decimal.from_float`, not decimal string approximations. This explains a conditional numerical mechanism, not a certified rounding-error budget, proof of the base provider or outer clamp/extension/wrapper, or a trace of individual machine instructions. The reported first differing intermediate is the first named recurrence intermediate compared, not necessarily the first operation that rounded. The legacy counterfactual changes all four terms together; individual term effects are not isolated.

The Decimal consistency check uses precision 100 for the comparison: `abs(recurrence - jet) <= 1e-90 * max(abs(recurrence), abs(jet), 1e-90)`. This is a numerical cross-check between two high-precision implementations, **not** a replacement for the 1e-9 relative gate, an output acceptance threshold, or an absolute floor in that gate. The indicated relative disagreement is the prior ledger’s original local-jet assessment, not the Decimal-consistency check. Cancellation is `(abs(base partial component) + abs(distance * Decimal normal derivative component)) / abs(Decimal output component)`; it concerns the final addition only, not a complete condition number or error bound. Infinite/undefined ratios are written explicitly if encountered.

The native diagnostic provenance is source commit `8ec4825280f7b2f9a41fc4183d609f8a080146e9`, published head `033e1885b652a5e32a88dc426ab1b97a97a8362d`, report SHA-256 `550f869523b049ae3e0bc3e3aaee1d004ff4678e1ccefee5b53e44e0836efc63`. Native reference library hashes matched historical build receipts, not a reproducible-build proof; no current integrated-head native run is asserted. See the preceding causal record for the inputs, trace context and four-term counterfactual.

Reproduction from the temporary attribution directory (Python standard library; no native builds):

```sh
python3 -B -m unittest -v test_rounding_probe
python3 -B rounding_probe.py
python3 -B generate_rounding_addendum.py
```

The `relative disagreement` column refers to the prior 80-digit ledger assessment.
